facts.fact: Name for the term on a Vietnamese shop's site: "Thức Ăn Đông Lạnh" (a product category).
The same shop also uses the category name "Mồi Tươi – Đông Lạnh".
Frozen foods are flash frozen to keep their nutrients and kill pathogens, and are sold as cubes or slabs.
After live food, frozen food comes closest to a wild diet, so picky eaters and fish with a poor appetite often take it.
Breeders use frozen foods to condition fish for spawning.
Frozen food feeds cleanly and does not dissolve into the water.
Bloodworms are midge fly larvae, red from natural hemoglobin. They suit meat-eaters such as betta (Betta), pufferfish and loaches, and come in regular, jumbo and mini sizes.
Brine shrimp (Artemia, about 1 cm) have a chitin shell that acts as roughage and helps fish such as goldfish, betta and Apistogramma avoid bloating and constipation.
Daphnia and cyclops (0.5–5 mm) suit nano fish and filter feeders. Baby brine shrimp (about 450 microns) suit fry.
Frozen tubifex worms (Tubifex) can help corydoras and other fish breed.
Herbivorous cichlids such as Mbuna need spirulina blends and should avoid high-protein worms. Shrimp should get frozen food only occasionally.
"Trùn huyết đông lạnh (Frozen Bloodworms)": a fresh food that is quickly frozen to keep its nutrients. Mayaqua lists it for betta, guppies, neon tetras, angelfish, discus, bottom-dwellers and shrimp.
"Trùng Huyết Đông Lạnh": its colour is listed as "Đỏ tươi / đỏ nâu" (bright red or reddish-brown).
"Trùn huyết" (also called "sâu đỏ") is the larva of Chironomid midges. The shop says it supplies iron because it contains haemoglobin.
"Trùng huyết (trùn huyết)" is described as the larva of a mosquito that lives in mud.
"Trùn Huyết Đông Lạnh Thức Ăn Cho Cá Cảnh" is a product name on a Vietnamese shop's list of frozen foods.
"Atermia Đông Lạnh Thức Ăn Cho Cá" is the frozen brine shrimp product name, spelled this way by the shop.
"Trùn chỉ đông lạnh" is a frozen food sold by Vietnamese shops.
"Lăng Quăng Đông Lạnh Thức Ăn Cá Cảnh" (frozen mosquito larvae) is a product name on a Vietnamese shop's frozen food list.
"Tim bò đông lạnh thức ăn cá cảnh" (frozen beef heart) is a product name on a Vietnamese shop's frozen food list.
"BOBO ĐÔNG LẠNH 100gr" is listed as "Cám chìm" (a sinking food) for "Cá nhỏ, Cá trung" (small and medium fish).
"Artemia đông lạnh" is sold by SaiGon Aqua in 200 g packs as food for ornamental shrimp and fish. The shop claims it is over 60% protein.
"Trùn chỉ đông lạnh" and "Trùn huyết đông lạnh" are suggested for predatory fish such as "hồng két" and "tai tượng", to stimulate their natural hunting reflexes.
English names used for the kinds: "Bloodworms", "Tubifex worms", "Brine shrimp", "Daphnia", "Baby brine shrimp" and "Mysis shrimp".
Direct method: put a cube or a piece of one in the tank, where it thaws quickly. A worm feeder cone slows its release and reduces mess.
Thawed method: thaw the food in a small jar of tank water for a few minutes, then feed it with a pipette or turkey baster to reach several tanks or target slow eaters.
"Trùng Huyết Đông Lạnh": cut off a small piece, soak it in tank water for about 1–2 minutes, then pour it into the tank. Or drop a small piece straight in for the fish to pick at.
Thaw one portion in a small cup of aquarium or dechlorinated water, drain off and throw away the thaw water, rinse the food, then feed small amounts.
"Trùng huyết": for frozen product, let it thaw naturally at room temperature. Rinse it until the water runs clear and drain it before feeding.
For picky eaters, thaw the food in a container without water and add a few drops of a vitamin supplement (the article uses Vita Chem).
Feed only what the fish finish within 2 to 3 minutes. About half a cube per feeding is typical for a 60 to 90 litre community tank.
"Trùng huyết": feed about 3–5 minutes' worth per meal, and cut the amount if the fish eat slowly or refuse food.
Typical omnivores and community fish can have frozen food from once a week to several times a week, alongside freeze-dried, gel, live and prepared foods.
"Trùng huyết": feed it 2–4 times a week, mixed with pellets, artemia or other dry food, according to one section of the page. Another section says 1–2 times a day.
Use frozen food a few times a week, use pellets or flakes the rest of the time, and give one fasting day per week.
Fish should have slightly rounded bellies: swollen bellies mean feed less, and sunken bellies mean feed more. A single betta may need only part of a bloodworm cube.
To move a fish that eats only frozen food onto pellets, mix pellets into the frozen food and raise the share of pellets bit by bit. Fasting for 2–7 days may make it more willing to try new food.
Keep the freezer at -18°C or below and store the food at the back, away from the door, where the temperature is steadier.
Split large packs into small portions, press the air out of the bags, and use the food within 6 to 12 months of manufacture.
"Trùng Huyết Đông Lạnh": keep it in the freezer at "-18°C trở xuống". It lasts "6 – 12 tháng nếu bảo quản tốt".
"Trùng Huyết Đông Lạnh": in a tank without a strong filter, do not feed it more than once a day. In shrimp tanks, clean up leftovers carefully.
Leaving frozen food at room temperature for more than about 30 minutes can make it spoil and smell.
Refreezing food that thawed at room temperature is a mistake, because bacteria may have grown in it.
Never refreeze fish food that has fully thawed.
Gensou counts dropping frozen cubes straight into the tank as a mistake that clouds the water and spikes ammonia. Aquarium Co-Op instead lists direct dropping as a normal method.
The thaw water contains phosphates and organics that can spike ammonia, so throw it away.
Common mistakes: overfeeding calorie-dense frozen food, feeding only one kind, using freezer-burned or expired food, and storing it near the freezer door.
If uneaten food is still on the bottom hours later, remove it and feed less next time.
"Trùng huyết": overfeeding can cause bloating and fouls the water.
"Trùng huyết": do not thaw it in hot water, and do not feed it while it is still icy.
"Trùng huyết": feeding it daily for a long time can upset digestion, and the fish may come to prefer it over pellets.
Keepers commenting on "trùng huyết đông lạnh" advise feeding only small pieces, because big amounts make the water cloudy.
A Vietnamese keeper reports that frozen worms carry a high risk of swim bladder inflammation ("viêm màng túi") in fish.
A Vietnamese keeper says the fattier "trùng chỉ" can spoil the body shape of fancy goldfish such as ranchu and telescope.
Bloodworm allergy is real for some fishkeepers. In a 2018 informal survey of 445 readers, about 34% reported a known or suspected allergy.
Dried bloodworms are anecdotally linked to more allergic reactions, but frozen or live worms can also trigger symptoms in sensitive people.
Allergic reactions to bloodworms range from rashes, which are frequent, to reactions that need emergency care. The median time before a keeper's first reaction was four years.
Keepers protect themselves from bloodworm allergy with gloves, feeding tongs, pre-portioned frozen blocks and face masks. Anyone with symptoms should seek medical advice.
Top Thủy Sinh sells "Artemia đông lạnh" but ships the frozen product only within Hanoi.
"Trùng huyết đông lạnh" is sold in Vietnam as a 200g zip bag ("túi zip") or as cubes ("viên") in 1 kg bags.

In Singapore's heat (28 to 34°C), frozen food thaws within about 2 to 5 minutes and should be used within about 30 minutes, because bacteria grow quickly above 25°C. This applies equally to Vietnam's tropical climate.
A Vietnamese shop warns that portions of frozen and fresh foods must be controlled to avoid polluting the tank water.
A Vietnamese shop's fry feeding guide says "Từ 7 ngày trở đi ăn bobo" (from 7 days old, feed bobo).
